_doc: Seconds each step of .github/workflows/pages.yml may take, keyed 'job/step name'. tools/step_budgets.py check-run fails the build job's last step on a step over its budget or with no row; tests/test_step_budgets.sh fails on a step with no row, and on a step that reads the whole corpus without naming the cache it restores ('cache'), how it limits itself to what changed ('incremental'), or why it can do neither ('uncached'). Raise a budget only with the reason in the commit: a budget that moves with every slowdown catches nothing.

build/Free disk space.note: added 10-30 after run 41138886134 died with No space left on device. The foreground delete of the image's .NET, Android, GHC and CodeQL bundles freed 18GB in 48-96s (runs 41143359058, 41157117731, the second over the old 90s budget), so it now runs in the background and the step only starts it: 10 is for df and the spawn

build/Check out.note: was 30. Two paths, measured over the last 100 runs of pages.yml (12 real build jobs): warm incremental fetch 9-12s (10 runs); and the store reset, where Check out finds the restored git store over 1500MB, drops .git and fetches from scratch, 91s and 94s (runs 40267913545, 40276271478). The store restarts at 335MB and grew to 1397MB and then 1660MB across the builds between resets, so the reset recurs about every 6th build (2 in 12): expected work, not runner variance, and it failed 2 of 12 builds against the old 30s. 150 = 1.6x the slowest reset seen (94s). The warm path is far under it (p99 12s); a warm-path regression now shows only as the step nearing 94s, which is the price of one row for both paths

build/Build the authored puzzle.note: 2s on a warm clue index (run 38378765553); 31s cold, which the explicit Save the clue index now prevents

build/Unpack the puzzle shims.note: untars the ~100k shims Restore the puzzle shims fetched as one file (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Warm the row cache, slice 1 of 8.note: was 60. Cold, all 8 slices took 61-66s in run 42542905051 (338f17b26f8 changed annotation.view, which every row reaches), not the ~40s once predicted here; an A/B of view() over 3270 clues with and without that change showed no per-row cost, so it is the cold corpus, not a regression. 80 = 1.2x the 66s max. build/Build the puzzle shims and reindex.note: 17-21s on warm shims and rows (runs 38378765553, 38385076152); 56-127s cold (127s in run 38390532020). Was 75, under that cold range: an edit to code the index rows reach (the format converter, run 38383021945) re-makes all ~51k rows by design and took 94s, so every such push went red for expected work. Was 150: 19-39s on 22 of 24 builds 2026-10-25..29 (median 31s), but a scheduled build reindexes every puzzle changed since the last deploy, and GitHub throttles the 15-minute cron to one build every few hours, so the batch is whatever the burn pushed meanwhile: 659 changed puzzles (twice any other batch seen) took 153s in run 40950475350. 190 = 1.2x that

build/Draw the social cards.note: was 360: a push touching tools re-listed every row and drew 120 cards in 368s (run 43223109759; 341s in run 43219464745 hours earlier), the worst case growing with the corpus; 450 = 1.22x 368. Was 900: the card key hashed make_og_card.py's bytes, so any edit redrew all ~17k cards 600 a run (816s, run 38370347047). Now keyed on the card's rendered HTML: steady state is the cached list (~15-40s) plus the cards a push moved; worst case a code edit re-lists every row (~60s) and draws OG_LIMIT=120 cards at ~0.9s each. Was 240: with a cold row cache the re-list took 146s and the 120 cards 100s (246s, run 39653095057), as the corpus grew. Was 300: a scheduled run after a day of annotate-code edits re-listed every row in 223s on a warm row cache, then drew 120 cards in 102s (329s, run 40199706228)

build/Unpack the puzzle pages.note: untars the ~42k pages and the page store Restore the puzzle pages fetched as one file (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Generate the crawlable pages, shar.note: was 6 shards, 93-96s on every one in the first cold build over 60k pages (run 42540698988: 9954 pages a shard, 84s of render plus 7s startup, ~8.4ms a page). 6 shards had been sized for ~62s cold on ~54k pages; corpus growth (+12%) and a higher per-page cost pushed a cold build over 90. Warm builds are 21-32s over 51 runs (max 32), so this bites only when a page-code change re-renders everything. All six shards were equal, so not runner variance: the answer is more shards, not a bigger budget. 9 shards of ~6.7k pages is ~63s cold, 1.4x under the unchanged 90s, room for ~40% more corpus before the next split. A ninth of the puzzle pages (--shard 0/9, by a hash of the id)

build/Choose the build path.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
build/Choose the build path.note: the puzzle fast path's test (tools/ci_scope.py against the last deployed commit): a few gh api calls and one blobless fetch of that commit's trees. Run 39360349916 spent 37s of its 37s in that fetch (no checkout; the log is silent until it prints), a base 82 paths behind: the fetch of a ~54k-file tree set grows with how far the deployed commit is, so 30s was too tight; 60s still catches a regression

build/Generate the crawlable pages (puzz.note: replaces the 8 warming slices, 6 page shards and Assemble on a push that only changed puzzle files (Choose the build path). The 4 shards plus the assemble took ~87s warm (run 39236355785) of which ~40s was workers piping each reused page's blocks back; build_seo_pages --reuse-first checks the stored pages in the parent and renders only the rest. Was 60, the assemble's: on the scheduled builds that deploy the burn's puzzle pushes it took 38-73s over 12 runs (2026-10-25..29), red in 3 (64, 64, 73s), and the time does not track the work: 1725 pages rendered in 51s (run 40609173036), 538 in 64s (run 40902755722). Runner variance on a fixed ~50s, so 90 = 1.2x the slowest 73s, the full path's shard budget. Raised to 150 on 2026-11-11: 10 puzzle-push runs 2026-11-12 (UTC) 01:04..04:45 took 73-137s warm (median 90.5s; 81, 77, 80, 85, 73, 137, 120, 96s) with two cold-cache outliers (511s, 545s); run 43154624689 went red at 96s with no change to build_seo_pages.py since 11-10 (its commit 0ea9595 only annotated one puzzle), so it is runner/load variance and growth of the corpus, not a regression. 150 = 1.1x the slowest warm 137s

build/Assemble the crawlable pages.note: was 60: 46-63s over 24 full builds 2026-11-04 (median 56, 63s in run 41801983040), no jump at any commit, so 80 = 1.25x the 63s max. The serial tail (hub, listings, sitemaps, ~10s of CPU) after the shards, and the check that every page was rendered by exactly one of them. Replaces the one 160s step, Generate the crawlable pages

build/List the site.uncached: lists the published files by glob; it opens none of them
build/List the site.note: was 20: 7-17s in 22 of 23 recent builds (median 11), 30s in one (the run after a cold render wrote ~138k files), so 20 sat 3s over the normal worst and failed on disk-cache luck, not a regression. 45 = 1.5x the 30s max. Globs PUBLISH and writes the tar list. Was Stage the site, 45s: 23s hard-linking ~138k files into _site/ and 22s checking links (run 38385716791)

build/Start the site checks.uncached: starts the checks Wait for the site checks collects, and returns
build/Start the site checks.note: only starts the link check and the IndexNow hashing in the background; their time shows in Wait for the site checks

build/Archive the site.note: was 60: 62s in run 43223109759 against 50s in run 43219464745 for the same artifact, a runner disk-read swing; 80 = 1.3x 62. Was 20. tar of a flat ~3.0GB artifact (3019-3034MB across 2026-11-04, so not growth): 7-16s on most of 24 builds but 22, 31, 31, 47, 28s on the last five (runs 41779499835, 41785869473, 41795828188, 41799841659, 41801983040), a disk-read swing between runners. 60 = 1.25x the 47s max

build/Upload the site.warn: actions/upload-artifact sending the stored (level 0) tar to GitHub, so the time is GitHub's upload and not our work: 26-40s over 21 push builds and 35-38s over 2 scheduled builds 2026-10-29..30 (median 35s, only 5s under the budget), with one 72s outlier (run 41005868629) for the same artifact; a 40s fail would go red on ordinary variance
build/Upload the site.note: 39s at deflate level 1 (run 38378765553), 65s at level 6; stored (level 0) 18s (run 38380967725)

build/Wait for the site checks.uncached: the link check reads every published page (stage_site.py --check, across the cores) and IndexNow hashes them; they run beside Archive and Upload, so this is only what is left over
build/Wait for the site checks.note: was the check half of Stage the site (22s) plus List the changed pages (8s), in series in front of the upload

build/Wait for the annotation check.warn: time spent waiting on the validate job, whose own steps (Check out, Choose what to check, each annotation shard) carry their own budgets in this same check; over 330 only on full checks (363s, 404s, 525s in runs 40902755722, 40583748046, 40724155380) with every validate step inside its budget, so the excess is outside any budgeted validate step (job start-up, runner queueing)
build/Wait for the annotation check.note: zero unless validate is still running when the build is ready, which only a full check does: validate then takes ~345s and the build reaches this step at ~190s since the cached checkout (124s in run 38380967725). Was 120 when the build was slower; covers a full check at its 300s budget. 219s in run 38636406433 (daily full check); 330 is 1.5x that

build/Deploy to Pages.warn: GitHub's Pages deploy: 71-437s over 24 builds 2026-10-25..29, over 180 in 5 (208, 334, 362, 437s on scheduled builds, 191s on a push) for the same ~2GB artifact; we only wait on GitHub here, and the artifact size is what we control (Upload the site, Archive the site)
build/Deploy to Pages.note: GitHub side: 69-134s (134s in run 38391832453, same artifact) for the 2.5GB, ~138k-file artifact (runs 38385076152, 38385716791, 38383021945); scales with what is shipped, not with what changed

build/Deploy to Pages (retry).warn: only runs after the first Deploy to Pages attempt stalled and was cut at 300s; the action's own 600s timeout bounds it
build/Deploy to Pages (retry).note: a stalled GitHub deploy (6 runs on 2026-11-07); a normal deploy never reaches this step

build/Pack the puzzle shims.note: tars puzzles/*.js, *.js.gz and shims.gz.json for Save the puzzle shims (tools/cache_tar.sh). Took 16-30s over the 7 builds before 10-22 (24s turned run 39811022168 red at the old 20s); grows with the corpus. Was 45: 23-29s on the scheduled builds 11-04..05, then 48s in run 42154127619 with no code change (Upload and Deploy slow in the same run too: a slow runner disk). 60 = 1.25x that

build/Pack the puzzle pages.note: runs only when Save the puzzle pages does; tars the pages for it (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Save the puzzle pages.note: runs only after a render of over 2000 pages (a code change, a cold cache)

scope/Check out.note: depth 1, blob:none, cone sparse to tools + .github/workflows: fetch ~15s (one 100k-entry tree) plus ~5s checkout. Was non-cone /tools/*.py patterns: 22s of checkout on top of the fetch, 33-41s in runs 41705181421, 41703010819, 41700482574, 41694862116

scope/Decide whether this run deploys.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
scope/Decide whether this run deploys.note: a puzzle-only push stops here and in validate (about a minute); the next scheduled tick deploys it. One gh api call for the live site's commit (tools/last_deploy.py); the blobless fetches of the parent and of the live commit run side by side (15-20s each, a whole tree), then the diff

validate/Check out.note: already depth 1, blob:none, sparse to tools + .github/workflows; still 65s and 74s (runs 38636406433, 38635950789) as the tools tree grew. 1.5x the observed 74s

validate/Choose what to check.note: a full check fetches the whole tree here, in eight streams (four until 2026-11-10); 155 is 1.2x the 129s worst of 34 full checks on 2026-11-10 (88-129s with four streams, the tree grown by the burn; over 110 in run 42870063495); the diff and the scope are a few seconds. Was 75: full checks took 67-89s on 2026-10-22 (89s in run 39799670301, 76s in the red run 39796038374); 110 is 1.2x the 89s

validate/Check every annotation, shard 1.note: a ninth of the puzzles (--shard 0/9, by a hash of the id). The step scales with the corpus divided by the shard count: add shards, never seconds. History: one step took ~315s against its 300s budget on 2026-10-17; four shards took 191-207s on 2026-10-23, so six (4/6 of ~200s is ~133s). On 2026-11-05 six shards went red in run 42020028035 (194-200s, over 190). Not corpus growth (11631 to 11643 puzzles per shard across the day's runs) and not a code change: across the last 21 validate runs (42011720380..42026742221) the per-run step time is bimodal, 99-145s in 8 runs and 195-212s in 13 (median 201s), alternating at random across commits and equal for all six shards within a run, i.e. a runner-speed lottery that is now mostly in its slow mode. So it is sized for the slow mode: 6/9 of ~200s is ~133s expected, 190 is 1.4x that
validate/Check every annotation, shard 1.uncached: the nightly and rule-change full check, spread across the runner's cores (validate_annotations.check_all); its budget is the alarm that the shards need splitting again
